---
title: "R cheat sheets"
subtitle: "MC 451 / MC 501 / MC 427 · every command, one explained on a page"
---

One page per package, covering every R command the worksheets, decks, and the R Companion use.
Each command gets a plain sentence, a worked example on the course Twitch data with the exact
output R prints, the same call rewritten for your own columns, and the error you are most likely
to hit. Every example below was run in R, and the output is pasted exactly as it printed.

## The sheets

| Sheet | What it covers |
|---|---|
| [readr](readr.qmd) ([PDF](readr.pdf)) | Read a file in and write one out: `read_csv()`, `write_csv()`, `read_rds()`, `write_rds()`, `clean_names()` |
| [dplyr](dplyr.qmd) ([PDF](dplyr.pdf)) | The verbs that reshape a table: `select()`, `filter()`, `mutate()`, `count()`, `group_by()` with `summarize()`, the joins, and the reshape helpers |
| [lubridate](lubridate.qmd) ([PDF](lubridate.pdf)) | Turn numbers and text into real dates: `as_datetime()`, `ymd_hms()`, `hour()`, `floor_date()` |
| [stringr](stringr.qmd) ([PDF](stringr.pdf)) | Measure and change text: `str_length()`, `str_detect()`, `str_replace()`, `str_glue()` |
| [ggplot2](ggplot2.qmd) ([PDF](ggplot2.pdf)) | Build a chart one layer at a time: `ggplot()`, `aes()`, the `geom_`s, `labs()`, `theme_v2v()` |
| [stats](stats.qmd) ([PDF](stats.pdf)) | Describe a variable and run a test: `t.test()`, `chisq.test()`, `aov()`, `lm()`, and the effect sizes |

## Every worksheet starts the same way

The first chunk of every worksheet loads the tools and the data. The examples on every sheet
assume these lines have already run:

```
library(tidyverse)    # dplyr, readr, stringr, lubridate, ggplot2, and more
library(v2v)           # the course package: the Twitch data and the course look
options(scipen = 10)  # long numbers, such as timestamps, print in full
```

The inferencing sheet also loads `library(effectsize)`, and the wrangling worksheet loads
`library(janitor)` for `clean_names()`. Each sheet lists the lines it needs at the top.

## How to read an entry

Every entry has the same shape:

- **A plain sentence** saying what the command does.
- **The code**, stacked one step per line, using the pipe `%>%` (read it as "and then").
- **The output**, exactly as R prints it after a real run.
- **On your data**, the same call written with plain column names you can copy.
- **If it breaks**, the error you are most likely to see and what it means.

## The data in the examples

Every example uses the course Twitch corpus from the `v2v` package: `twitch_chat()` is one row per
chat message, `twitch_streams()` is one row per stream snapshot, and `twitch_channels()` describes
each channel. Here are five messages, so you can picture the data the examples work on:

```
twitch_chat() %>%
  select(channel, sender, message) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5)
```

```
# A tibble: 5 × 3
  channel    sender       message
  <chr>      <chr>        <chr>
1 sodapoppin madzee       ???????????????????????
2 xqcow      prometheanow TriEasy Clap TriEasy Clap TriEasy Clap TriEasy Cl…
3 forsen     spectre155   cmonBruh
4 sodapoppin itsjer       sodaTHINKING
5 xqcow      laserfruit   @xQcOW PLAY JACKBOX PARTY GAMES PLAY JACKBOX PART…
```

Where an example needs the joined analysis table, it starts from `analysis`, the table the Data
Wrangling worksheet builds by joining the three together.
